title: SIEM Bridge: fanout, ack model, and durable delivery paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a resilient SIEM Bridge service that reliably fans out audit events to third-party sinks (Splunk HEC, Datadog Events/Logs, customer webhooks) and Redwood-internal audit sinks. The service must provide clear delivery guarantees, observability, and operator controls in Console. Key outcomes: durable buffering, configurable ack model, idempotency support, selective per-tenant routing, and safe admin controls via RBAC v2.
background_and_motivation: Customers with enterprise logging requirements need proof they receive all audit events in their SIEMs. Current ad-hoc webhook delivery lacks durable buffering and tenant-scoped retry policies. This work reduces incident volume for missed audit deliveries, supports compliance requests, and unlocks enterprise contracts that require vendor-to-SIEM guarantees.
goal: Implement a general-purpose SIEM Bridge (connector) architecture, with at-least-once delivery with configurable dedup/ids for near-exactly-once behavior, per-tenant queues, DLQ, telemetry (latency, attempts, DLQ rate), and Console controls for routing, retry policy, and key rotation. Provide connectors for Splunk HEC and Datadog as first-class targets and a generic webhook sink with HMAC signing.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Events are stored durably in an internal tenant-scoped queue before delivery.
2) Webhook and Splunk connectors support idempotency tokens to suppress duplicates.
3) Delivery SLOs documented and enforced: 99.9% of events delivered within 120s under steady-state load; 99.99% for internal sinks.
4) DLQ created and accessible in Console; DLQ rate <0.05% in normal operation.
5) Retry policy configurable per-tenant with exponential backoff + jitter and max TTL.
6) Admins with RBAC v2 permission "audit.sink.manage" can add/update connectors; others cannot.
7) End-to-end encryption/signing: webhooks signed (HMAC) and Splunk HEC keys stored in KMS.
8) End-to-end tests and chaos test (broker restart/DB failover) prove no silent loss in >1M event run.
9) Dashboard with token-level cost and failure breakdown and an incident runbook linked.
design_decisions:
- Use a small durable write-ahead log (WAL) per-tenant in our existing events-store for buffering.
- Delivery workers will use an ack/commit model: worker pulls batch -> attempts -> on success commit sequence -> on failure return to queue with backoff metadata.
- Idempotency: surface an event-id header; for sinks that support idempotency (Splunk HEC idempotency token, Datadog dedupe) we set and rotate tokens; otherwise maintain a per-destination recently-seen cache for a short window.
- DLQ: store failed events with failure reason, HTTP response code, and last attempt timestamp; expose actions: requeue, redact-and-send, delete.
- Security: Connector credentials encrypted with KMS and audited via RBAC v2; only principals with audit.sink.manage can mutate connectors.
- Observability: metrics (delivery_latency_ms/p50,p95,p99, attempts, dlq_rate), traces with sampling for slow/failing deliveries, and per-tenant alert rules.
- Trade-offs: exact-once semantics across remote third-party systems is impossible; we provide idempotency primitives and tooling to achieve practical near-exactly-once for common SIEMs.
implementation_tasks:
1) Schema: add destination and delivery metadata to audit event model (ENG-20420).
2) Persistence: WAL/queue integration with events-store; migration plan for existing events (ENG-20422).
3) Worker: implement delivery workers with concurrent per-tenant rate limits and in-flight caps.
4) Connectors: Splunk HEC connector (HEC idempotency token support), Datadog Logs/Events connector, Generic Webhook with HMAC signing.
5) Console: UI to add connectors, view DLQ, set retry policies and routing rules.
6) RBAC: ensure audit.sink.* perms enforced in Console and API.
7) KMS: key rotation support and credential ownership audit logs.
8) Tests: unit, integration, chaos, and a 1M event E2E test.
9) Docs & Runbook: PRD update, operator runbook for incidents, and customer-facing docs on delivery guarantees.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Bursting tenants can cause unbounded queue growth. Mitigation: per-tenant burst tokens and configurable retention TTL; apply backpressure via 429 and circuit-breaker.
Risk: Third-party sink rate limits cause prolonged retries. Mitigation: per-destination throttling, adaptive backoff, and human-notify when queue grows beyond threshold.
Risk: Secret compromise. Mitigation: KMS + limited operator RBAC + key rotation + audit trails.
Risk: Misconfigured retry policies causing duplicate flood. Mitigation: provide sane defaults, warn in Console when polcies deviate from recommended.
qa_and_test_plan:
- Unit tests for worker ack/commit and idempotency checks.
- Integration tests against Splunk HEC test instance and Datadog sandbox.
- E2E test runs with synthetic events: 1M events across 50 tenants, random sink failures, and verification that DLQ/requeue produce expected outcomes.
- Chaos testing: simulated events-store restart and KMS unavailability during delivery.
- Security review: static analysis, credential leakage scan, and RBAC enforcement tests.
release_notes: Add SIEM Bridge service (beta) with Splunk and Datadog connectors, tenant-scoped durable buffering, DLQ UI, per-tenant retry policies, HMAC webhook signing, and RBAC v2 admin controls. Beta customers may opt-in; data residency and KMS options supported for Private deployments.
